newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EURO LEAGUE SOME WAY OFF SAYS MAN UTD'S EDWARDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EURO LEAGUE SOME WAY OFF SAYS MAN UTD'S EDWARDS.

text.p: A fully-fledged European soccer league is not likely to become a reality for some time, Manchester United chief executive Martin Edwards said on Monday.
"I personally believe that a European super league is some way off...I don't see it as an immediate thing," Edwards said.

The European Cup Champions' League will be expanded next season to include 24 teams rather than 16. They will play in six groups of four, the six group winners and two top runners-up progressing to a knockout competition.
Edwards said that UEFA's decision to revise the Champions' League format indicated that a full-blown league was not in the offing.
Speaking to reporters in a telephone conference call, Edwards confirmed that English champions United would like to see the 20-club premier league trimmed to 18 teams.
"We would prefer an 18-club premier league. It would ease our programme especially if we're going to be involved in Europe," he said.
"It is very, very difficult to be successful in Europe when we're playing so many games."
However, other premier league clubs are strongly opposed to a reduction, fearing the loss of revenue from fewer games and the risk of failing to remain in the elite.
Edwards said that only United and Arsenal voted for a cut the last time the issue was raised.
United, top of the league and in the semifinals of the European Cup, are arguing for an extension to the English season to ease their fixture congestion.
United's success as a business was illustrated again on Monday when the club announced that profit for the six months to January totalled 19.5 million pounds ($31.9 million).

Bigger crowds at the club's redeveloped Old Trafford stadium and higher television revenue helped the English champions to lift turnover by 68 percent to 50.1 million pounds in the six months to the end of January.
Edwards said the club's run to the last four of the European Cup had earned it around 7.5 million pounds. United play Germany's Borussia Dortmund in a semifinal first leg on Wednesday.

United's gate receipts increased to 18.4 million pounds from 10.4 million following the completion of rebuilding at Old Trafford. Average home crowds topped 54,000 whereas they had been limited to 37,000 while the work was being done.
Edwards said the club would increase its ticket prices by an average of five to six percent next season.
